audit_notes: v1.0.1: S08 gold reduced to the single Frost Control chunk that contains the default timed-exhaust 5-minute / 30-minute behavior; the previously listed second chunk primarily describes electric preheat / modulating-wheel text and was not necessary evidence for that question.
v1.0.1: Added difficulty labels on supported scenarios (direct_terminology | natural_paraphrase | indirect_reference | multi_evidence).
v1.0.1: Added companion holdout paraphrase file greenheck_erv_eval_v1_holdout_paraphrase.json; original S01–S14 IDs preserved.
pdf_sha256_note: content_sha256 equals the full local PDF file SHA-256 for this revision.
excluded_page_rationale: Page 31 is a flattened Symptom/Possible Cause/Corrective Action troubleshooting table; extraction loses column alignment and is unreliable for grounded retrieval.
chunking_note: Eligible narrative chunks only; page 31 never indexed. Chunk IDs embed a content-hash prefix and change if the PDF bytes change.
creation_criteria: Every supported fact was verified against eligible chunks from pages 15, 29, or 33 of the local PDF.
No LLM-generated answer was treated as ground truth.
Unsupported cases either lack indexed evidence, depend on excluded page 31, or are blocked by the prototype operational-safety policy.
Adversarial items are labeled separately and must not use the production chunk index as gold evidence.
Dataset stores paraphrased reference facts only; long copyrighted manual passages are not republished.
known_limitations: Only three eligible pages from one product manual; not a general HVAC QA benchmark.
Semantic neighbors may retrieve related frost/filter text for unsupported queries; neighbors are not proof of support.
Operational-policy abstention is an application gate, not a measure of model grounding quality.
Chunk boundaries can split multi-sentence procedures across IDs; gold lists may include multiple Frost Control chunks.
External filter size table rows on page 29 are sparse and only lightly used as gold.

scenarios.question: What does the dirty filter sensor monitor?
reference_facts_paraphrased: Dirty filter sensors monitor pressure drop across outdoor air filters, exhaust air filters, or both.
forbidden_claims: Exact replacement filter OEM part numbers
Factory dirty-filter switch set point values
scenarios.rationale: Directly stated in the Dirty Filter Sensor section on page 15.

scenarios.question: What happens when the dirty filter pressure drop exceeds the set point?
reference_facts_paraphrased: If pressure drop exceeds the set point, the sensor closes contacts in the unit control center for a field-wired alarm/light.
forbidden_claims: Factory-set pressure threshold numeric value
scenarios.rationale: Contact-closing behavior is described on page 15 Dirty Filter Sensor.

scenarios.question: Where is the dirty filter switch mounted?
reference_facts_paraphrased: Mounted in the exhaust inlet compartment next to the unit control center, or in the unit control center.
scenarios.rationale: Mounting location is stated in the Dirty Filter Sensor section.

scenarios.question: Why is frost control used on the energy recovery wheel?
reference_facts_paraphrased: Cold outdoor air can cause moisture condensation and frosting on the energy recovery wheel; frost control is an optional feature to prevent/control wheel frosting.
forbidden_claims: Claiming frost control is mandatory on every unit
scenarios.rationale: Purpose and optional nature are on page 15 Frost Control intro.

scenarios.question: What frost control options are available?
reference_facts_paraphrased: Three options: timed exhaust, electric preheat, and modulating wheel frost control.
scenarios.rationale: Option list appears in Frost Control on page 15.

scenarios.question: Which sensors must trigger before frost control starts?
reference_facts_paraphrased: Both the outdoor-air thermodisc and the wheel pressure sensor must trigger to initiate frost control.
scenarios.rationale: Dual-sensor initiation requirement is stated on page 15.

scenarios.question: What outdoor air temperature indication is associated with frost occurring?
reference_facts_paraphrased: Outdoor air temperature below 5°F together with increased pressure drop indicates frost may be occurring.
forbidden_claims: Treating 5°F alone as sufficient without the pressure condition
scenarios.rationale: Temperature and pressure pairing is on page 15 Frost Control.

scenarios.question: How does timed exhaust frost control behave with the default timer setting?
reference_facts_paraphrased: Default timed exhaust shuts down the supply fan for 5 minutes every 30 minutes to allow exhaust to defrost the wheel.
scenarios.rationale: Default timer behavior (5 minutes every 30 minutes) is contained in Frost Control chunk p15:c1. v1.0.1 removed p15:c2 from gold because that chunk continues into electric-preheat / modulating-wheel text rather than the timed-exhaust timer fact.

scenarios.question: What does electric preheat frost control do when initiated?
reference_facts_paraphrased: An electric heater at the outdoor air intake turns on to warm air entering the energy wheel and avoid frosting.
scenarios.rationale: Electric preheat behavior is on page 15.

scenarios.question: How does modulating wheel frost control change wheel speed?
reference_facts_paraphrased: A VFD reduces wheel speed when frost conditions are met; reduced effectiveness keeps exhaust from reaching saturation.
scenarios.rationale: Modulating wheel / VFD behavior is on page 15 Frost Control.

scenarios.question: Where is the microprocessor controller located and how is an alarm indicated?
reference_facts_paraphrased: The microprocessor is in the main control center; in alarm the alarm button blinks red and a message appears on the screen.
forbidden_claims: Detailed DDC fault-code meanings from the separate DDC manual
scenarios.rationale: Microprocessor Controller section on page 33.

scenarios.question: What does the rotation sensor monitor?
reference_facts_paraphrased: It monitors energy wheel rotation and closes contacts if the wheel stops rotating.
scenarios.rationale: Rotation Sensor section on page 15.

scenarios.question: What does the manual say about internal filter maintenance?
reference_facts_paraphrased: Units typically use 2-inch thick pleated paper filters that should be checked on a routine schedule and replaced as necessary for proper airflow.
forbidden_claims: Exact manufacturer filter SKU / part number
scenarios.rationale: Internal Filter maintenance guidance is on page 29.

scenarios.question: How often should coils be checked under normal operating conditions?
reference_facts_paraphrased: Check coils once per year under normal operating conditions; clean if dirty by brushing or vacuuming.
scenarios.rationale: Coil inspection interval is on page 29 Coils.

scenarios.question: What is the exact OEM replacement part number for the outdoor air filter?
forbidden_claims: Inventing a specific filter part number
scenarios.rationale: Eligible pages discuss filter types/maintenance but do not give an outdoor-air filter OEM SKU.
